title: Since 2008 NOAA CoralTemp follows the Met Office OSTIA analysis to 0.01 C; its late-2020 step is the OSTIA v3.4 upgrade of 8 December 2020, which also steps ERA5 SST by +0.04 C against Argo
abstract: Question: NOAA Coral Reef Watch CoralTemp v3.1 has mean steps in January 2008 and late 2020 (five campaign studies), but their causes and the late-2020 date were not known, and two studies disagreed about a 2020 step in ERA5. After 2002, CoralTemp is the NOAA Geo-Polar Blended Night analysis, which corrects satellite biases to the Met Office OSTIA analysis. Approach: we compared daily OSTIA near-real-time (NRT) and Geo-Polar files (NCEI GHRSST archive), CoralTemp, ERA5 and DOISST on one 0.25-degree grid, read the OSTIA product_version of each file, and tested steps against Argo near-surface data, which OSTIA does not use. Results: on 187 sampled days of 2008-2023, CoralTemp minus OSTIA NRT is -0.001 C (SD 0.010 C, 30S-30N); before 2008 the SD is 0.098 C. On 1 January 2008 CoralTemp rises by +0.046 C against Argo (95% interval 0.033 to 0.059) and joins OSTIA NRT, which does not change (-0.017 C). OSTIA NRT changes from version 3.3 to 3.4 on 8 December 2020, when the Met Office added SLSTR to its bias-correction reference. On that day OSTIA, Geo-Polar (= CoralTemp) and ERA5 step by +0.034, +0.038 and +0.042 C against Argo (intervals 0.027-0.049), and by +0.040 to +0.044 C against DOISST (30S-30N). A control date (8 December 2018) and the OSTIA v3.3 date (4 December 2019) give +0.001 to +0.005 C, and the earlier proposed date 4 November 2020 gives no step. The upgrade halves the cold offset of all three products relative to Argo (-0.07 to -0.04 C). The first day of OSTIA v3.0 (13 February 2018) is the date of an unexplained ERA5 variance step, but its mean step is small (+0.010 C). Thus the post-2002 CoralTemp homogenisation needs two dated causes, and ERA5 SST anomalies after 8 December 2020 contain about +0.04 C from the OSTIA upgrade. Limitations: Argo tests cover 30-60 days around each date; DOISST-based tests share DOISST noise; the pre-2008 bias reference (first OSTIA reanalysis) was not available; DHW was not recomputed.

(a) Steps against Argo (not used by OSTIA), 30 days each side, with 95% bootstrap intervals: 1 January 2008, OSTIA v3.0 (13 Feb 2018), a control date, OSTIA v3.3 (4 Dec 2019) and OSTIA v3.4 (8 Dec 2020). (b) Steps against DOISST at candidate dates (30S-30N).
